business_problem: Roma Capitale needed to modernize a decades-old document-management environment and create a central data platform that could ingest many kinds of city data and support services for millions of citizens, commuters, and tourists.
solution_summary: Roma Capitale used MongoDB Enterprise Advanced to modernize its electronic document-management system and build a city data platform for smart-city services. The prior GED environment ran on a proprietary relational database and made it hard for engineers to work with the transport details, legal documents, welfare records, and other diverse datasets the city needed to combine. MongoDB's flexible document model let the team ingest that mixed data, keep it in a centralized platform, and query it in real time across portals, online services, and internal applications. The system now manages more than 110 million documents and keeps growing, which makes scalability and operational simplicity critical for a relatively small engineering team. Because those records sit in one readable and queryable environment, Roma Capitale can use the platform for citizen services and for urgent operational needs, such as the citywide healthcare and welfare response during the Coronavirus period.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Enterprise Advanced
solution_components.role: Stores Rome's mixed civic data and powers the central document and smart-city data platform used across services.

data_flow: Transport details, legal documents, welfare records, and other city data are ingested into MongoDB Enterprise Advanced, unified on one platform, and then queried in real time by portals, applications, and public-service workflows across Rome.
business_outcome: MongoDB gave Roma Capitale a scalable city data platform that improved service efficiency, supported real-time access to integrated records, and strengthened smart-city operations for residents and visitors.
